standard_prerequisites.name: Finite flat is finite locally free

core_obligations: From the scheme-version splitting, note s', t' are finite locally free, so t(s^{-1}(u')) is a finite set of points.
Take quasi-compact W containing them; W -> U quasi-compact (U affine), locally quasi-finite and separated, hence W quasi-affine by the ZMT variant.
Use ampleness to find an affine open containing the finite set, then the invariant-affine lemma to shrink to a P-invariant affine U'' containing u'.

Verify P|_{U''} is still a strong splitting of R|_{U''}: P invariant means the restrictions of s'' and t'' to P|_{U''} stay finite, and conditions (a), (b), (c) persist since the self-arrow set over u' is unchanged.
proof_roadmap: Finite-locally-free bookkeeping, ZMT quasi-affineness, invariant-affine shrink, and the splitting-property persistence check.
difficulty_reason: Four genuine steps with two non-trivial external inputs (ZMT variant, invariant affine open) and a persistence verification.
